lines.say: This is a chat with a travel assistant. Your first message says you are allergic to peanuts.
cues: Your first message says you are allergic to peanuts.

lines.say: The model doesn't see words. It sees tokens: small pieces of text. This message is twenty of them.
cues: The model sees tokens. This message is twenty of them.

lines.say: And it keeps nothing between turns. Every time you send a message, the app sends the whole conversation again, and the model reads all of it, from the top.
cues: The whole conversation is sent again, every turn.

lines.say: But one request can only hold so many tokens. That limit is the context window.
cues: One request can only hold so many tokens.

lines.say: Ours holds a hundred and eight. Real ones hold hundreds of thousands, and long conversations fill those too.

lines.say: When the next message doesn't fit, something has to go. Usually, the oldest turn. The one about peanuts.

lines.say: Peanut satay. Your message is still on your screen. It just wasn't in what the model was sent.

lines.say: There are three common fixes. First, pin the important facts at the front, so they are always sent.
cues: Pin the important facts at the front.

lines.say: Second, summarise old turns before they are dropped.
cues: Summarise old turns before they are dropped.

lines.say: Third, store them outside the window, and fetch back the ones that match the new question.
